correctness.rationale: For degree at most two, a selected endpoint with one active neighbor halves its incident distance; with two active neighbors the triangle inequality bounds the new incident distance by (epsilon+2epsilon)/3. Unselected edges are unchanged. For every degree >=3 a scalar star-neighborhood configuration immediately breaks one active edge. On fully active cycles the local exact energy drop equals 4/9 times the squared Laplacian coordinate; Fourier eigenvalues give the sharp uniform \(1-16\sin^2(\pi/n)/(9n)\) factor, attained by a scaled first harmonic. Iterated expectation and Markov give the stated first-hitting-time tail. The included checker verifies 163105 exact first steps and 84000 exact further updates, and numerical spectral comparisons; only the proof extends beyond finite tests.

value.rationale: The new theorem completely classifies every finite social topology on which bounded-confidence ties never rupture, a directly motivated invariant in fragmented-opinion systems. It locates the sharp structural phase boundary at the first degree-three branch, bounds the number of topology events deterministically, and supplies a size-dependent exact optimal one-step contraction factor and geometric approximate-consensus tail on cycles; it is a natural infinite-family classification rather than a preset or isolated finite invariant.
